card: This PR implements BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup) validation rules in Bitcoin Core, configured as active exclusively on regtest and never active on mainnet, testnet, and signet. It mitigates quadratic legacy sigops CPU exhaustion, blocks timewarp and negative difficulty retargeting, enforces coinbase height timelocks, and rejects 64-byte transactions to prevent Merkle tree collisions. Approximately 95% of the line additions consist of test vectors, unit tests, a fuzzing target, and functional tests ported and refined from Bitcoin Inquisition. It enables testing and review of consensus cleanup logic without altering live network consensus.
changed_since_previous: Rebased without architectural changes; maintains regtest-only activation and BIP 54 validation rules while updating test adjustments.

enables: Regtest testing and potential future deployment of BIP 54 on public networks

evidence: PR description: 'Roughly 95% of the added lines are tests or test data... The bip54_tests unit test module exercises each mitigation extensively in isolation. The feature_bip54.py functional test verifies all of them end-to-end after and prior to activation.'

Commit 25e9699b9f note on consensus behavior: 'When BIP54 is active, enforce that block transactions do not violate the BIP54 limit on the number of legacy sigops present in Scripts that get executed during block validation.'
Commit 689f45ae12: '64-byte transactions are invalid (BIP 54) due to serious flaws in the Merkle tree algorithm that make it so that such transactions may be re-interpreted as inner tree nodes.'
problem: Bitcoin consensus retains vulnerabilities to timewarp difficulty manipulation, negative difficulty adjustment periods, Merkle tree collisions from 64-byte transactions (CVE-2017-12842), and legacy sigops validation CPU exhaustion. Bitcoin Core currently has no implementation or test suite for the BIP 54 rules, preventing testing and evaluation of the consensus cleanup package within the repository.

risk.why: A flaw in the consensus checks or versionbits deployment parameters could cause a chain split or prematurely invalidate valid blocks.

scope_notes: Roughly 5,800 lines of the ~6,500 lines added are test vectors and JSON fixtures (such as bip54_timestamps.json and bip54_coinbases.json) and unit/functional test files.
summary: Implements the BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup) validation rules across transaction verification and block header validation, enabling them exclusively on regtest via BIP 9 versionbits deployment bit 3 while setting them to never active on mainnet, testnet, and signet. The rules constrain difficulty adjustment period timestamps to block timewarp and Murch–Zawy attacks, require coinbase transactions to be timelocked to block height minus one, restrict non-witness sigops per transaction to 2,500, and invalidate 64-byte transactions to prevent Merkle tree leaf-internal node ambiguity. Over 95% of the added lines consist of unit tests, JSON test vectors, fuzz harnesses, and end-to-end functional test coverage.
